title: Unimark Ivory — One-Word Typographic Monument
description: A single concept word set at 70% canvas height in Helvetica dominates an ivory field — no decoration, no images, only cobalt type and black metadata clustered in the bottom-left corner. Vignelli's severity, undiluted.
philosophy: This template exists because the word itself is the entire argument. It refuses color blocks, iconography, and multi-weight hierarchies — scale, tracking, and silence are the only variables permitted. It is built for speakers who trust a single noun to carry a room: a brand launch, a manifesto title, a conference theme declaration. Decoration here is not merely restrained; it is structurally impossible by design.
goodFor: Conference keynote title slides built around one anchoring concept word
Brand launch reveals where the name itself is the entire message
Design, architecture, or typography industry presentations
Gallery opening or exhibition programme title slides
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring data visualization
Multi-point agenda or bullet-list instructional slides
Pitch decks needing financial tables or comparative diagrams
Workshops with step-by-step procedural content across many slides
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide is a typographic monument: one word commands authority over an unbroken luminous field through scale alone — no imagery, geometry, or competing rhythm. Mood is Vignelli-severe Swiss rationalism, where silence and tracking carry all meaning. Compositional tension comes from the asymmetric relationship between the colossal word mass and the small metadata cluster anchored at lower left. Avoid softness, ornamentation, or layered hierarchy that dilutes the word's singular weight.

examples.layoutNotes: Single dominant word occupies cols 1–11 of a 12-col grid, ranged left against a consistent left-edge margin, scaled to fill roughly 70% of canvas height. No header band, rule line, or decorative element interrupts the field above or to the right. Metadata block — deck context, event line, or date — clusters tightly in the bottom-left corner at a dramatically smaller scale, hugging the baseline grid. Right and top margins remain entirely silent; letter-spacing of the word is the sole spatial variable permitted.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads as a typographic broadsheet pinned to a gallery wall — one word commands the space while a whispered secondary line below it acts as a footnote, not a headline. The mood is glacial and declarative: Swiss modernist severity kept intact even as the slide carries actual content. Compositional rhythm is asymmetric-but-anchored, with the left margin rail acting as the single spine all elements hang from. Avoid any softening gestures — no rules, no tints, no iconography; tension lives entirely in the scale gap between the monument word and everything else.

examples.layoutNotes: Flush-left grid with a wide breathing margin on the right (roughly 35% of canvas width left as void). The primary concept word anchors the upper-center zone at near-full monument scale, left-aligned to the same margin rail as all other elements. A single secondary line — a terse sub-concept, attribution, or definition fragment — sits below with a deep vertical gap, distinguished by tracking contrast alone, not weight or size jump. Page number and contextual metadata remain pinned as a tight cluster in the bottom-left corner, isolated from the word by pure negative space.
